verifications.note: Energy Transfer LP FY2018 Form 10-K, 'Acquisition of HPC': 'ETO previously owned a 49.99% interest in HPC, which owns RIGS. In April 2018, ETO acquired the remaining 50.01% interest in HPC. Prior to April 2018, HPC was reflected as an unconsolidated affiliate in ETO's financial statements; beginning in April 2018, RIGS is reflected as a wholly-owned subsidiary in ETO's financial statements.' HPC = RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co., defined in the same filing's glossary as 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co. and its wholly-owned subsidiary, Regency Intrastate Gas LP', and RIGS = 'Regency Intrastate Gas System' -- i.e. this pipeline. States the value recorded on the row (100% owned, single owner) as of April 2018 onward.

Energy Transfer Operating, L.P. FY2018 Form 10-K, same 'Acquisition of HPC' disclosure verbatim (ETO is the direct owner of record; ET LP is ETO's public parent) -- confirms ETO (Energy Transfer's operating partnership, the 'ETP legacy' entity) held a 100% interest in HPC/RIGS beginning April 2018, same wording as the ET LP filing since ETO is the primary reporting entity being consolidated into ET.

resolutions.researcher_notes:
Recorded value (Owner1='ETP Legacy', Owner1%='100.00%', single owner, no Owner2+) is CONFIRMED as of April 2018 onward by both of ETO's own FY2018 10-Ks (parent Energy Transfer LP, CIK 1276187, and the direct owning subsidiary Energy Transfer Operating LP, CIK 1161154): ETO acquired the remaining 50.01% of HPC (RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co., which owns the RIGS system) in April 2018, having previously held only 49.99%; RIGS has been reflected as a wholly-owned (100%) subsidiary of ETO ever since. Tier=high on the primary/regulatory-source-alone rule in confidence_tiers.md (audited SEC Form 10-K) even though both filings share near-identical boilerplate language and are not independent of one another (same corporate family/disclosure control -- marked independent=false accordingly, not to be read as two separate confirmations). Third-party corroboration found but NOT included as a proposed_ref because it fails scripts/url_verifier.py's name-match check (it names 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co.' and 'a gas pipeline in Louisiana' but never 'Regency' or 'Regency Intrastate'): Astatine Investment Partners (successor to Alinda Capital Partners' fund manager) lists 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co.' as an Exited investment and states 'Fund II sold its 50% interest in RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co., which owned a gas pipeline in Louisiana, to Energy Transfer Partners in 2018' (https://astatineip.com/investment/rigs-haynesville-partnership-co/) -- independently corroborates the counterparty side of the same April 2018 transaction from the seller's (Alinda's) own disclosure, not Energy Transfer's.

HISTORY (context only, not needed to source the current cell but explains why 100% is right and not a data error): the pipeline was never solely ETP-owned before 2018. Predecessor Regency Intrastate Gas LLC was wholly Regency-owned through 2005 (per the row's existing SEC 10-K and Google Books FEIS refs, which cover the 'Enhancement Project' segment's original 2005 construction). In March 2009 Regency contributed the whole RIGS system's equity into a new joint venture, RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co. ('HPC'), alongside Alinda Gas Pipeline I/II, L.P. (Alinda Investors) and EFS Haynesville, LLC (GE Energy Financial Services affiliate) -- confirmed by the row's existing SEC exhibit dex992.htm (audited HPC financial statements, FY2010/2009): Regency HIG got a 38% GP interest, EFS Haynesville 12%, Alinda 50%. Regency increased to 43% in Sept 2009 (bought 5% from EFS); by FY2016 Energy Transfer Partners' own 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1012569/000101256917000022/etp12-31x201610k.htm) states 'We own a 49.99% interest in HPC' -- i.e. through 2009-April 2018 this pipeline was a JV, NOT 100% ETP-owned, ending at 49.99% ETP / ~50.01% Alinda+EFS. That JV was unwound in April 2018 (ETO bought out the remaining 50.01%), which is the event the two 2018 10-Ks above document and which brings the row's 100%-single-owner value back into agreement with the primary sources. Nothing here contradicts the sheet -- it confirms the current cell and explains the pre-2018 JV years a naive search would otherwise surface as a false conflict.
